title: At-Tariq 86:1-4 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 2: Al-A'la, At-Tariq 1 to 8 and waqf
source: Written for quran/y5 lesson 27 (Pupil PDF worksheet: At-Tariq 86:1-4 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 27. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلطَّارِقِ (١) وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلطَّارِقُ (٢) ٱلنَّجْمُ ٱلثَّاقِبُ (٣) إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌۭ (٤)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: By the sky and the night comer -
And what can make you know what is the night comer?
There is no soul but that it has over it a protector.

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Madd muttasil; sun letters س and ط
Silent laams; doubled ن and ث
Idgham without ghunnah: tanween into ل

keywords.def: the night comer, a bright star

questions.q: Chunk and link At-Tariq 86:1-4 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 86:1-4 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 86:1-4 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: On the pupil PDF, circle the sun-letter laams in 86:1 to 3.
Explain why stars are a good sign to think about.
questions.a: Allah made them bright in the dark sky, for light, direction and beauty: they show His power.

questions.q: What is 'the night comer' (at-tariq) explained as in 86:3?
questions.a: A) The piercing star. 86:3: 'It is the piercing star.'

questions.q: Think again: Allah swears by a bright star that pierces the darkness. Then He says every soul has a protector over it (86:4). Who might that protector be?
questions.a: Angels whom Allah has set to watch over and record each person: nothing we do is unseen.
